body.heading: The pause is not the story
paragraphs: Illness, travel, busy seasons, plain discouragement: every long project collects pauses. The pause feels like the end only because restarting has its own awkward first step.
Notice the unhelpful thought that you must 'catch up' or restart at full speed. You do not owe the project a penalty. You only owe it a next step.

body.heading: Restart at half size
paragraphs: Return with a deliberately smaller version: half the time, half the distance, the easiest section first. A gentle restart protects the habit from the soreness, literal or otherwise, of doing too much too soon.
Mark the restart day somehow: a note in the calendar, a line in your log. Future pauses will be easier once you have evidence that you are a person who comes back.

takeaway: Come back at half size, without penalties, and let the habit warm up again.
